proofs.proof_tex:
Choose distinct labels \(1,2\in\mathcal J\), which is possible because \(J\geq2\), and choose a unit vector \(e\in\mathbb R^q\), which is possible because \(q\geq1\). Fix \(c\in(0,H]\). Define
\[
 h^{(0)}_1=0,\qquad h^{(0)}_j=ce\quad(j\ne1),
\]
and
\[
 h^{(1)}_2=0,\qquad h^{(1)}_j=ce\quad(j\ne2).
\]
For every \(\Delta>0\), use the same effect vector at both states:
\[
 b^{(\Delta)}_1=0,\qquad b^{(\Delta)}_2=\Delta,
 \qquad b^{(\Delta)}_j=0\quad(j\geq3).
\]
Each \((h^{(\ell)},b^{(\Delta)})\), \(\ell\in\{0,1\}\), belongs to \(\mathcal H_H\). Indeed, every score norm is either zero or \(c\leq H\), each state has exactly one zero-score label, and hence the coherence implication for two zero-score labels is vacuous. By the definition of \(\tau(h,b)\),
\[
 \tau(h^{(0)},b^{(\Delta)})=0,
 \qquad
 \tau(h^{(1)},b^{(\Delta)})=\Delta.
 \tag{1}
\]

Let \(m_{\ell,c,\Delta}\in\mathbb R^p\) be the interleaved mean of \(Z^{\mathrm{pan}}\) under state \(\ell\), and set
\[
 d_c=m_{1,c,\Delta}-m_{0,c,\Delta},
 \qquad
 \rho_c=(d_c^{\top}\Omega^{-1}d_c)^{1/2}.
 \tag{2}
\]
Positive definiteness of \(\Omega\) makes \(\Omega^{-1}\) and \(\Omega^{-1/2}\) well defined. Because the effect vector is identical at the two states, all effect-coordinate differences cancel. The first two score-block differences are respectively \(ce\) and \(-ce\), and all remaining score-block differences are zero. Thus \(d_c=cd_1\) for a fixed nonzero vector \(d_1\), so
\[
 \rho_c=c(d_1^{\top}\Omega^{-1}d_1)^{1/2}\longrightarrow0
 \qquad(c\downarrow0).
 \tag{3}
\]
In particular, \(\rho_c\) is independent of \(\Delta\).

Write \(P_{\ell,c,\Delta}=N(m_{\ell,c,\Delta},\Omega)\). Both laws have positive Lebesgue densities. For \(\rho_c>0\), transform an observation \(z\) to
\[
 x=\Omega^{-1/2}\left(z-\frac{m_{0,c,\Delta}+m_{1,c,\Delta}}2\right),
 \qquad
 u=\frac{\Omega^{-1/2}d_c}{\rho_c}.
\]
Then \(\lVert u\rVert_2=1\), the likelihood ratio is at least one exactly when \(u^{\top}x\geq0\), and \(u^{\top}x\) is \(N(-\rho_c/2,1)\) under state zero and \(N(\rho_c/2,1)\) under state one. Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \lVert P_{0,c,\Delta}-P_{1,c,\Delta}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}
 &=P_{1,c,\Delta}\{u^{\top}x\geq0\}
   -P_{0,c,\Delta}\{u^{\top}x\geq0\}\\
 &=\Phi(\rho_c/2)-\Phi(-\rho_c/2)
 =2\Phi(\rho_c/2)-1
 =:v_c.
\end{aligned}
\tag{4}
\]

Let \(K\) be any measurable confidence kernel satisfying the honesty constraint in the definition of \(\mathfrak R_{\alpha}^{G}(H,\Omega)\). Let \(Q_{\ell,c,\Delta}\) be the joint law of the observation and the reported random set after applying \(K\) to \(P_{\ell,c,\Delta}\). A Markov kernel contracts total variation: for every measurable event \(A\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 |Q_{1,c,\Delta}(A)-Q_{0,c,\Delta}(A)|
 &=\left|\int K(z,A_z)\,d(P_{1,c,\Delta}-P_{0,c,\Delta})(z)\right|\\
 &\leq \lVert P_{1,c,\Delta}-P_{0,c,\Delta}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}
 =v_c,
\end{aligned}
\tag{5}
\]
because \(0\leq K(z,A_z)\leq1\). Define
\[
 A_0=\{(z,C):0\in C\},
 \qquad
 A_1=\{(z,C):\Delta\in C\}.
\]
Membership of both states in \(\mathcal H_H\), honesty, and (1) imply
\[
 Q_{0,c,\Delta}(A_0)\geq1-\alpha,
 \qquad
 Q_{1,c,\Delta}(A_1)\geq1-\alpha.
 \tag{6}
\]
Equation (5) gives \(Q_{0,c,\Delta}(A_1)\geq1-\alpha-v_c\). Hence the union bound gives
\[
 Q_{0,c,\Delta}(A_0\cap A_1)
 \geq1-2\alpha-v_c.
 \tag{7}
\]
On \(A_0\cap A_1\), the reported set contains both \(0\) and \(\Delta\), so its diameter is at least \(\Delta\). Consequently,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sup_{(h,b)\in\mathcal H_H}
 \mathbb E_{h,b,\Omega}[\operatorname{diam}(K(Z^{\mathrm{pan}}))]
 &\geq
 \mathbb E_{h^{(0)},b^{(\Delta)},\Omega}
 [\operatorname{diam}(K(Z^{\mathrm{pan}}))]\\
 &\geq \Delta\,Q_{0,c,\Delta}(A_0\cap A_1)\\
 &\geq \Delta[1-2\alpha-v_c].
\end{aligned}
\tag{8}
\]
When the bracket is negative, the last inequality remains valid because diameter is nonnegative.

By (3), continuity of \(\Phi\), and \(\Phi(0)=1/2\), one has \(v_c\to0\) as \(c\downarrow0\). Since \(0<\alpha<1/2\) and \(H>0\), there is \(c_0\in(0,H]\) such that \(1-2\alpha-v_c>0\) for every \(c\in(0,c_0]\). Fix one such \(c\). Inequality (8) then holds for every \(\Delta>0\) with the same positive multiplier. The definition of \(\mathcal H_H\) imposes no bound on the spread of \(b\), so letting \(\Delta\to\infty\) shows that every honest kernel has infinite worst-case expected diameter. Taking the infimum over honest kernels yields
\[
 \mathfrak R_{\alpha}^{G}(H,\Omega)=+\infty.
\]
Thus neither a finite frontier nor a finite-valued attaining program exists on the frozen full Gaussian face space.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(0<\alpha<1/2\). Let \(P_0=N(\mu_0,\Gamma)\) and \(P_1=N(\mu_1,\Gamma)\) be Gaussian score laws on \(\mathbb R^{Jq}\) with \(\Gamma\in\mathbb S_{++}^{Jq}\), let their target values be \(\tau_0,\tau_1\in\mathbb R\), and put \(\Delta=|\tau_1-\tau_0|>0\) and \(\rho=((\mu_1-\mu_0)^{\top}\Gamma^{-1}(\mu_1-\mu_0))^{1/2}>0\). Among all measurable confidence kernels satisfying \(P_\ell\{\tau_\ell\in K\}\geq1-\alpha\) for \(\ell=0,1\),
\[
 \inf_K\max_{\ell\in\{0,1\}}
 \mathbb E_{P_\ell}[\operatorname{diam}(K)]
 =\Delta[\Phi(z_{1-\alpha}-\rho)-\alpha]_+.
\]
The value is attained by the likelihood-ratio acceptance regions
\[
 A_0=\{T\leq-\rho/2+z_{1-\alpha}\},
 \qquad
 A_1=\{T\geq\rho/2-z_{1-\alpha}\},
\]
where
\[
 T=\frac{(\mu_1-\mu_0)^{\top}\Gamma^{-1}
 (X^{\mathrm{sc}}-(\mu_0+\mu_1)/2)}{\rho},
 \qquad
 K^*(X^{\mathrm{sc}})=
 \{\tau_0:X^{\mathrm{sc}}\in A_0\}\cup
 \{\tau_1:X^{\mathrm{sc}}\in A_1\}.
\]
In particular, the exact value is zero if and only if \(\rho\geq2z_{1-\alpha}\). For the identity-covariance two-donor switch \(\mu_0=(0,c)^{\top}\), \(\mu_1=(c,0)^{\top}\), one has \(\rho=\sqrt2c\). If two such states with a common exactly observed \(b\) form a restriction of \(\mathcal H_{H,B}^{\mathrm{sc}}\), then
\[
 \mathfrak R_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{sc}}(H,B,\Gamma)
 \geq\Delta[\Phi(z_{1-\alpha}-\rho)-\alpha]_+.
\]
For every \(J\geq1\), including faces with several zero-score labels and arbitrary shared-control covariance \(\Gamma\),
\[
 0\leq\mathfrak R_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{sc}}(H,B,\Gamma)\leq B.
\]
The upper bound is delivered by the simultaneous score-screen hull
\[
 K_{\mathrm{scr}}(x,b)
 =\operatorname{conv}\left\{b_j:
 \lVert\Gamma_{jj}^{-1/2}x_j\rVert_2\leq k_{1-\alpha}^{\mathrm{sc}}(\Gamma)
 \right\},
\]
with the empty hull interpreted as empty, where \(\Gamma_{jj}\) is the \(j\)-th principal score block and \(k_{1-\alpha}^{\mathrm{sc}}(\Gamma)\) is the \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile of \(\max_{j\in\mathcal J}\lVert\Gamma_{jj}^{-1/2}G_j\rVert_2\) for \(G\sim N(0,\Gamma)\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Write \(d=\mu_1-\mu_0\). Positive definiteness of \(\Gamma\) implies that \(\Gamma^{-1}\) exists and that \(\rho>0\) is well defined. For
\[
 T=\frac{d^{\top}\Gamma^{-1}(X^{\mathrm{sc}}-(\mu_0+\mu_1)/2)}{\rho},
\]
direct calculation gives
\[
 T\sim N(-\rho/2,1)\quad\text{under }P_0,
 \qquad
 T\sim N(\rho/2,1)\quad\text{under }P_1,
 \tag{9}
\]
and the likelihood ratio is \(dP_1/dP_0=\exp(\rho T)\).

We first derive the necessary testing inequality. Put
\[
 t_0=-\rho/2+z_{1-\alpha},
 \qquad D^*=\{T>t_0\}.
\]
By (9), \(P_0(D^*)=\alpha\) and
\[
 P_1(D^*)=1-\Phi(z_{1-\alpha}-\rho)=\Phi(\rho-z_{1-\alpha}).
 \tag{10}
\]
If \(D\) is any measurable, possibly randomized event with \(P_0(D)\leq\alpha\), let \(k=\exp(\rho t_0)\). Because \(f_1-kf_0\) is nonpositive off \(D^*\) and nonnegative on \(D^*\),
\[
 (\mathbf 1_D-\mathbf 1_{D^*})(f_1-kf_0)\leq0
\]
pointwise on the observation space augmented by any state-independent randomization variable. Integration and \(P_0(D)\leq P_0(D^*)\) give
\[
 P_1(D)-P_1(D^*)
 \leq k\{P_0(D)-P_0(D^*)\}\leq0.
 \tag{11}
\]
Thus (10) is the largest state-one probability of an event having state-zero probability at most \(\alpha\); this conclusion was derived directly from likelihood-ratio ordering.

Now let \(K\) be any confidence kernel satisfying the two coverage constraints, and define the inclusion events
\[
 A_0=\{\tau_0\in K\},
 \qquad A_1=\{\tau_1\in K\},
 \qquad O=A_0\cap A_1.
\]
The event \(D=A_1\setminus A_0\) obeys
\[
 P_0(D)\leq P_0(A_0^c)\leq\alpha
\]
and
\[
 P_1(D)=P_1(A_1)-P_1(O)geq1-\alpha-P_1(O).
\]
Applying (11) yields
\[
 P_1(O)\geq1-\alpha-\Phi(\rho-z_{1-\alpha})
 =\Phi(z_{1-\alpha}-\rho)-\alpha.
 \tag{12}
\]
On \(O\), the set \(K\) contains both target values and therefore has diameter at least \(\Delta\). Nonnegativity of diameter and (12) imply
\[
 \max_{\ell\in\{0,1\}}
 \mathbb E_{P_\ell}[\operatorname{diam}(K)]
 \geq\Delta[\Phi(z_{1-\alpha}-\rho)-\alpha]_+.
 \tag{13}
\]

For attainability, take the displayed regions \(A_0\) and \(A_1\) and report exactly the corresponding subset of \(\{\tau_0,\tau_1\}\). Equation (9) gives \(P_0(A_0)=P_1(A_1)=1-\alpha\). Their intersection is empty up to a null boundary when
\(
 \rho/2-z_{1-\alpha}\geq-\rho/2+z_{1-\alpha}
\), equivalently \(\rho\geq2z_{1-\alpha}\). In that case the risk is zero. If \(\rho<2z_{1-\alpha}\), then under state zero
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P_0(A_0\cap A_1)
 &=\Phi(z_{1-\alpha})-\Phi(\rho-z_{1-\alpha})\\
 &=\Phi(z_{1-\alpha}-\rho)-\alpha,
\end{aligned}
\tag{14}
\]
and the same calculation under state one gives the same probability. The rule's diameter is exactly \(\Delta\) on the intersection and zero otherwise, so (14) attains (13). Since \(0<\alpha<1/2\) implies \(z_{1-\alpha}>0\), the positive-part expression vanishes exactly at and above \(2z_{1-\alpha}\). For \(\Gamma=I_2\), \(\mu_0=(0,c)^{\top}\), and \(\mu_1=(c,0)^{\top}\), direct substitution gives \(\rho=(c^2+c^2)^{1/2}=\sqrt2c\).

Suppose next that the two states, with the same exactly observed \(b\), are contained in \(\mathcal H_{H,B}^{\mathrm{sc}}\). Any kernel honest on the full score-face space is honest at those two states, and its supremum risk over the full space is at least its maximum risk over the pair. Taking the infimum over full-space kernels and using (13)--(14) proves the displayed general-\(J\) lower bound by restriction.

It remains to prove the finite upper bound. Partition \(G\sim N(0,\Gamma)\) and \(X^{\mathrm{sc}}\) into their \(q\)-dimensional label blocks. Every principal block \(\Gamma_{jj}\) is positive definite because \(\Gamma\) is positive definite, so \(\Gamma_{jj}^{-1/2}\) exists. Define
\[
 M=\max_{j\in\mathcal J}
 \lVert\Gamma_{jj}^{-1/2}G_j\rVert_2.
\]
The random variable \(M\) is finite almost surely. Its distribution is continuous because \(G\) has a Lebesgue density and every level set of any nonconstant quadratic norm has Lebesgue measure zero. Hence the finite quantile \(k_{1-\alpha}^{\mathrm{sc}}(\Gamma)\) in the statement satisfies
\[
 \Pr\{M\leq k_{1-\alpha}^{\mathrm{sc}}(\Gamma)\}=1-\alpha.
 \tag{15}
\]
Use the displayed score-screen hull. Under parameter \((h,b)\), the centered vector \(X^{\mathrm{sc}}-h\) has the same joint law as \(G\), including all covariance induced by shared controls. On the event in (15), every label with \(h_j=0\) is screened in. The definition of \(\mathcal H_{H,B}^{\mathrm{sc}}\) guarantees at least one such label, and its coherence restriction guarantees that every such label has value \(\tau(h,b)\). Therefore
\[
 \Pr_{h,\Gamma}\{\tau(h,b)\in K_{\mathrm{scr}}(X^{\mathrm{sc}},b)\}
 \geq1-\alpha
\]
uniformly over \((h,b)\in\mathcal H_{H,B}^{\mathrm{sc}}\), including faces with several zero-score labels. Because the accepted values form a subset of \(\{b_1,\ldots,b_J\}\), the spread restriction gives, for every observation,
\[
 \operatorname{diam}\{K_{\mathrm{scr}}(X^{\mathrm{sc}},b)\}
 \leq \max_j b_j-\min_j b_j\leq B.
\]
The screen is measurable because it is determined by finitely many continuous inequalities, and the finite convex hull has measurable minimum and maximum endpoints on each acceptance pattern. Thus it is an admissible confidence kernel, proving \(\mathfrak R_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{sc}}(H,B,\Gamma)\leq B\). The lower bound by zero follows from nonnegativity of diameter.
added_lemmas.justification: This theorem gives the exact two-state honest expected-diameter value in the correctly scaled score-only experiment and supplies computable lower and upper bounds for the multiple-face problem.
added_lemmas.gap: The two-state constant is derived directly from Gaussian likelihood-ratio ordering; the exact minimax constant over a general finite union of donor faces remains unresolved.
added_lemmas.consumer: It makes the identity-covariance switch result a corollary, supplies an inherited lower bound for every embedded donor switch, and certifies the finite upper bound \(B\) under arbitrary shared-control covariance.

proposed.name: Abstract coherent Gaussian donor-face space \(\mathcal H_H\)
proposed.construction: \(\mathcal H_H=\{(h,b)\in(\mathbb R^q)^J\times\mathbb R^J:\min_{j\in\mathcal J}\lVert h_j\rVert_2=0,\ \max_{j\in\mathcal J}\lVert h_j\rVert_2\leq H,\ h_j=h_k=0\Rightarrow b_j=b_k\}\). The final implication is an additional abstract Gaussian coherence restriction; it is not a consequence of the zero-score equalities alone.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The definition must quarantine its coherence implication as an independent abstract restriction.

proposed.name: Bounded-spread score-only donor-face space \(\mathcal H_{H,B}^{\mathrm{sc}}\)
proposed.construction:
\[
 \mathcal H_{H,B}^{\mathrm{sc}}
 =\left\{(h,b)\in(\mathbb R^q)^J\times\mathbb R^J:
 \min_{j\in\mathcal J}\lVert h_j\rVert_2=0,\ 
 \max_{j\in\mathcal J}\lVert h_j\rVert_2\leq H,\ 
 \max_{j\in\mathcal J}b_j-\min_{j\in\mathcal J}b_j\leq B,\ 
 h_j=h_k=0\Rightarrow b_j=b_k
 \right\}.
\]
Only the spread of \(b\) is bounded; no restriction is placed on its absolute location.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Bounding effect spread is the minimal explicit repair that blocks the escaping \(\Delta\to\infty\) sequence while preserving unrestricted absolute location.

proposed.name: Score-only honest expected-diameter frontier
proposed.construction:
In the score-only experiment one observes \((X^{\mathrm{sc}},b)\), where \(X^{\mathrm{sc}}\sim N(h,\Gamma)\) and \(b\) is observed without noise. Define
\[
 \mathfrak R_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{sc}}(H,B,\Gamma)
 =\inf_K\sup_{(h,b)\in\mathcal H_{H,B}^{\mathrm{sc}}}
 \mathbb E_{h,\Gamma}
 \left[\operatorname{diam}(K(X^{\mathrm{sc}},b))\right],
\]
where the infimum is over measurable confidence kernels
\(K:\mathbb R^{Jq}\times\mathbb R^J\rightsquigarrow2^{\mathbb R}\) satisfying
\[
 \inf_{(h,b)\in\mathcal H_{H,B}^{\mathrm{sc}}}
 \Pr_{h,\Gamma}\!\left\{\tau(h,b)\in K(X^{\mathrm{sc}},b)\right\}
 \geq1-\alpha.
\]

proposed_core_edits.reason: The correctly scaled limit observes unscaled post-effect means exactly and retains Gaussian noise only in the root-sample-scaled scores.

proposed.name: Score-face primal and proposed decision-dual handle
proposed.construction:
For the score-only experiment, the primal variables are measurable randomized confidence kernels \(K:\mathbb R^{Jq}\times\mathbb R^J\rightsquigarrow2^{\mathbb R}\). Their constraints are
\[
 \Pr_{h,\Gamma}\{\tau(h,b)\in K(X^{\mathrm{sc}},b)\}\geq1-\alpha
 \quad\text{for every }(h,b)\in\mathcal H_{H,B}^{\mathrm{sc}},
\]
and their objective is
\[
 \sup_{(h,b)\in\mathcal H_{H,B}^{\mathrm{sc}}}
 \mathbb E_{h,\Gamma}[\operatorname{diam}(K(X^{\mathrm{sc}},b))].
\]
Acceptance-region duality may be used as a proposed route to this program only after domination, joint measurability in the face parameter, and a valid reduction from expected fixed-measure loss to expected diameter have been proved. No such reduction is included in this definition.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The optimization handle must expose its kernel variables, coverage constraints, and diameter objective, while treating published expected-measure duality only as a template until the missing reductions are proved.

proposed.name: Restricted score-only reduced-experiment transfer handle
proposed.construction: A correctly scaled transfer attempt compares the reduced mean experiment \(\mathcal E_n^{\mathrm{mean}}\) only with the score-only limit that observes \(b\) exactly and observes \(X^{\mathrm{sc}}\sim N(h,\Gamma)\). It must construct Markov kernels in both directions whose deficiencies tend to zero uniformly on a specified dominated compact QMD submodel, and it must separately prove uniform integrability for the diameter losses before transferring expected risk. The previously proposed target with fixed Gaussian noise in the unscaled effect coordinates is excluded by the scaling obstruction. This handle asserts no equivalence: domination, product measurability, uniform likelihood-process approximation, and the expected-risk transfer remain proof obligations.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The refuted fixed-noise effect-coordinate recipe must be replaced by the score-only target with exact observation of \(b\), while leaving deficiency and loss-transfer conditions as explicit obligations.

proposed.statement: In the explicitly two-dimensional observation experiment \(Z^{\mathrm{sw}}\), the minimum over all confidence kernels \(K:\mathbb R^2\rightsquigarrow2^{\{0,\Delta\}}\) satisfying \(\min_{\ell\in\{0,1\}}\Pr_{\ell}\{\ell\Delta\in K(Z^{\mathrm{sw}})\}\geq1-\alpha\) of \(\max_{\ell\in\{0,1\}}\mathbb E_{\ell}[\operatorname{diam}(K(Z^{\mathrm{sw}}))]\) is \(r_2(c,\Delta,\alpha)=\Delta[\Phi(z_{1-\alpha}-\sqrt2c)-\alpha]_+\). The rule \(C^{\mathrm{NP}}_{c,\Delta,\alpha}\) attains this value, including the zero-overlap regime. Under the \(J=2\), \(q=1\) panel submodel with \(b=(0,\Delta)^{\top}\), \(L_{\mathrm{sw}}\Omega L_{\mathrm{sw}}^{\top}=I_2\), and state-invariant independent \(U^{\mathrm{sw}}\), the full observation \(Z^{\mathrm{pan}}\) is equivalent to the switch experiment augmented by an ancillary variable, so the same minimax value and rule apply.
proposed.justification: The identity-covariance formula is the \(\rho=\sqrt2c\) corollary of the general two-state Mahalanobis result, with the independent ancillary factor establishing the panel embedding.
proposed.gap: The exact two-donor problem is closed; only the exact minimax constant over general finite donor-face unions remains open.
proposed.consumer: The corollary calibrates the early kill test and quantifies the gap between likelihood-ratio inversion and the maximum-critical benchmark.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Its identity-covariance formula is now explicitly a corollary of the Mahalanobis two-state theorem; the ancillary-coordinate panel extension remains in place.

proposed_core_edits.proposed: \(C_n^{\mathrm{proj}}(\alpha)=\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_{j\in\mathcal J}I_{j,n}(\alpha))\) is the feasible simultaneous projected confidence set. On the unrestricted-effect full Gaussian face space, \(\mathfrak R_{\alpha}^{G}(H,\Omega)=+\infty\). The finite repaired weak-separation benchmark is the score-only value \(\mathfrak R_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{sc}}(H,B,\Gamma)\), which observes \(b\) exactly and bounds only its spread.
proposed_core_edits.reason: The old metadata incorrectly advertised the infinite full Gaussian risk as an optimal finite benchmark; it must distinguish the valid projected confidence set, the infinite obstruction, and the bounded score-only benchmark.

Few-treated-group inference with many controls is distinct from inference driven by many micro observations within a fixed finite set of labels.

Global asymptotic equivalence requires substantially stronger domination, smoothness, positivity, compactness, and likelihood-process control than the panel moment assumptions provide.

prose_updates.tldr: A finite menu of prespecified donor stacks creates nonregular inference when validity is defined by an exact zero of a noisy baseline score. The panel confidence procedures remain causal only under the explicit nonempty exact-close condition and the shared-slope additive untreated-change condition; zero score alone does not imply target coherence in the abstract Gaussian limit. The unrestricted-effect full Gaussian frontier is infinite. The finite repair mandated by this obstruction observes the unscaled donor effects exactly, keeps Gaussian noise only in the root-sample-scaled scores, and bounds their spread by \(B\) while leaving absolute location unrestricted. Its two-state value is exactly \(\Delta[\Phi(z_{1-\alpha}-\rho)-\alpha]_+\), with a zero-diameter elbow at \(\rho=2z_{1-\alpha}\); a simultaneous score-screen hull gives the general finite bound \(B\), while the exact general-face constant remains open. None of these conditional results validates the historical CMS comparison-state estimates.

project_justification.gap: Existing few-treated panel and synthetic-control methods do not solve honest expected-diameter inference when a valid donor label is defined by an exact zero score and several labels may lie on the same face. Generic post-selection results also do not determine the minimax constant for this discontinuous target map.
project_justification.niche: The CMS comparison-state workflow has finitely many candidate labels, many beneficiaries within each state, unequal sample sizes, reused controls, and uncertainty about exact transport. A causal conclusion requires an exact population equality plus a model connecting the score to untreated changes. Ranked empirical balance supplies neither, and the abstract implication from zero scores to a common effect is an additional restriction rather than an algebraic fact.
project_justification.fill: The project proves exact-close transport under the explicit shared-slope untreated-change model, gives uniformly honest simultaneous and pilot-adaptive procedures with fixed-separation oracle behavior, proves that the originally frozen full Gaussian frontier is infinite when effect spread is unrestricted, and supplies the bounded-spread score-only repair. The repaired experiment has an exact two-state Mahalanobis minimax formula, a general embedded-pair lower bound, and a simultaneous-screen upper bound \(B\); only the exact general finite-face constant and a fully justified finite-sample-to-score-only risk transfer remain open.

sampling_model.design: There are fixed finite treated groups and prespecified donor stacks. Each donor stack has known comparison-group weights, and its score is the treated-minus-donor contrast in the prespecified baseline levels, pre-period slopes, and case-mix summaries contained in \(G_{ri}\). Exact population equality, not ranked sample proximity, defines a close donor.
sampling_model.units: At each \(n\), observations are independent within and across the fixed primitive groups under the product law \(\mathbb P_n=\bigotimes_{r\in\mathcal R}P_{r,n}^{\otimes n_r}\), with every limiting group fraction bounded away from zero. Shared treated groups and reused controls induce non-diagonal score covariance and are retained in \(\Gamma\).
sampling_model.treatment: Treatment is a fixed realized group-level history. Consistency identifies observed post outcomes with the corresponding potential outcomes. Causal transport additionally requires the nonempty exact-close condition and the additive untreated-change condition \(\mathbb E[Y_{ri}(0)-Y_{ri}^{\mathrm{pre}}\mid G_{ri}]=\kappa_n+\beta_n^{\top}G_{ri}\); these are substantive crux assumptions, not consequences of Gaussian approximation.
sampling_model.overlap: Every primitive group has a limiting sample fraction bounded away from zero. No treatment-propensity overlap condition is invoked, but the finite donor menu must contain at least one exact population-close label in every law under which causal coverage is claimed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Group means and within-group covariance matrices are estimated directly, and the known contrast matrix propagates covariance from shared treated groups and reused controls. Spectral clipping totalizes the feasible panel inversions. In the corrected local decision experiment, only the root-sample-scaled score vector has Gaussian noise; the unscaled donor-effect vector is observed exactly, and its spread is bounded by \(B\).

prose_updates.related_work: The reviewed RTI material describes the CMS comparison-state workflow through ranked baseline distance, retained comparison states, claims-driven substitutions, and person-level weighting; it does not document ex ante algebraic calibration to known population totals for every score component. Hence the workflow is a motivating and falsifiable use case, not evidence that the paper's exact-close assumptions held historically. Conley and Taber and Ferman and Pinto obtain reference variation from many control groups, unlike the many-within-group, fixed-label regime here. Chernozhukov, Wuthrich, and Zhu study time-series synthetic-control inference rather than exact donor-face uncertainty. Berk et al. motivate simultaneous protection but do not establish minimaxity of the maximum-critical hull. Andrews, Kitagawa, and McCloskey study argmax-winner selection; the present exact-zero-face model is not their argmax-selection model, and neither parameter class contains the other without changing both the selection rule and the estimand. Their work motivates the separate pilot-adaptive oracle construction only. Evans, Hansen, and Stark supply an acceptance-region expected-measure template, but their duality is not used as a theorem here because domination, product measurability, and the reduction from fixed sigma-finite expected measure to expected diameter have not been proved. Andrews and Cheng, Andrews and Mikusheva, and Nussbaum motivate weak-limit and experiment-comparison questions but do not remove the effect-coordinate scaling obstruction or establish the required score-only risk transfer.
prose_updates.interpretation: The infinite full Gaussian frontier is an ill-posedness diagnosis, not a failure of simultaneous panel coverage: with unrestricted \(b\), nearly indistinguishable score faces can select effects separated by arbitrarily large \(\Delta\). The bounded score-only experiment isolates the economically relevant weak-separation cost after ordinary post-mean noise has vanished. Exact two-face adaptation is governed by Mahalanobis score separation, while a covariance-aware simultaneous screen remains valid on multiple-zero faces. For the CMS workflow, the operational implication is to prespecify and audit exact calibration and untreated-trend transport; good ranked balance cannot be substituted for either condition.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The unrestricted-effect full Gaussian benchmark has minimax expected diameter \(+\infty\), so no finite general program can attain it. The repaired score-only bounded-spread experiment has an exact two-state value and the finite general bound \(0\leq\mathfrak R_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{sc}}(H,B,\Gamma)\leq B\), including shared-control covariance and multiple-zero faces, but its exact general-\(J\) constant is not derived. Evans--Hansen--Stark duality remains only a template because the necessary domination, joint measurability, and expected-measure-to-diameter reduction are absent. Likewise, finite-sample transfer is claimed only after a future proof of two-sided uniform deficiency and uniform integrability for the score-only loss; the refuted fixed-noise effect-coordinate target is excluded. The accepted pilot-adaptive construction and its oracle-equivalence statement are unchanged.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Uniform causal coverage and fixed-separation oracle conclusions apply only to the triangular-array panel class satisfying consistency, stable group fractions, moment and covariance regularity, a nonempty exact close set, and the shared-slope additive untreated-change condition. In the abstract Gaussian face problems, equality of the \(b_j\) values at simultaneous zero-score labels is separately imposed and is not implied by \(h_j=0\). The original unrestricted-effect full Gaussian frontier is infinite. Finite weak-separation risk statements concern the corrected score-only experiment with exactly observed \(b\), positive definite \(\Gamma\), and spread at most \(B\); the exact theorem covers any two embedded faces and the simultaneous screen covers general finite faces, but exact general-face minimaxity and Le Cam risk transfer are not claimed. No reviewed source establishes the exact calibration assumptions for the historical CMS estimates.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem identifies the precise maximality failure of the original Gaussian benchmark: unrestricted effect spread permits arbitrarily distant targets on score faces whose laws become arbitrarily close.
statement_notes.gap: A finite frontier cannot exist on the frozen class; the bounded-spread score-only experiment is therefore a separate corrected problem rather than a reinterpretation of the infinite value.
statement_notes.consumer: The obstruction determines which effect-coordinate scaling and spread restriction every valid weak-separation frontier must use.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem solves the minimal donor-switch problem exactly and remains valid under arbitrary positive definite score covariance through Mahalanobis reduction.
statement_notes.gap: It yields restriction lower bounds and a finite simultaneous-screen upper bound, but not the exact constant for every general finite union of donor faces.
statement_notes.consumer: It calibrates the identity-covariance corollary and provides the computable benchmark for future general-face optimization.

statement_notes.justification: The identity-covariance result is the \(\rho=\sqrt2c\) specialization of the Mahalanobis theorem, together with the already proved ancillary-coordinate panel equivalence.
statement_notes.gap: The two-donor switch is solved; it does not imply that a maximum-critical hull is optimal on larger face unions.
statement_notes.consumer: It supplies the exact early-kill-test value and the benchmark used by the maximum-hull comparison.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem shows that unscaled donor-effect estimates become asymptotically revealing and therefore cannot converge to a Gaussian limit retaining fixed effect-coordinate noise.
statement_notes.gap: It rules out the old target but does not prove two-sided deficiency or expected-risk transfer for the corrected score-only experiment.
statement_notes.consumer: The result forces every future transfer theorem to observe \(b\) exactly or to rescale a genuinely local effect parameter.

proofs.proof_tex:
Write \(\widehat b_n=(\widehat b_{1,n},\ldots,\widehat b_{J,n})^{\top}\), and let \((\Omega_n)_{bb}\) denote the principal submatrix of \(\Omega_n\) indexed by the \(J\) effect coordinates.  Let \(\mathbb E_{n,\eta}\) and \(\operatorname{Var}_{n,\eta}\) denote expectation and variance under \(\mathbb P_{n,\eta}\).  The exact mean--covariance calculation underlying \(\mathrm{lem:joint\text{-}gaussian}\), obtained from the constructions in \(\mathrm{def:stacked\text{-}estimator}\) and \(\mathrm{def:shared\text{-}covariance\text{-}estimator}\) and from independence of the primitive groups in \(\mathrm{def:panel\text{-}model\text{-}class}\), gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{n,\eta}[\widehat\theta_n]=\theta_n,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_{n,\eta}(\widehat\theta_n)
 =A\operatorname{diag}_{r\in\mathcal R}
   \left(\frac{\Sigma_{r,n}}{n_r}\right)A^{\top}
 =\frac{\Omega_n}{n}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \mathbb E_{n,\eta}[\widehat b_n]=b_n,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_{n,\eta}(\widehat b_n)
 =\frac{(\Omega_n)_{bb}}{n},
 \tag{1}
\]
where \(b_n=(b_{1,n},\ldots,b_{J,n})^{\top}\).  This calculation also shows explicitly that shared treated or donor groups induce the off-diagonal entries of \((\Omega_n)_{bb}\); no independence across donor labels is asserted or needed.

Fix the two parameters in the statement and put
\[
 d_b=\|b^{(1)}-b^{(0)}\|_2>0,
 \qquad
 u=\frac{b^{(1)}-b^{(0)}}{d_b},
 \qquad
 t=\frac{u^{\top}b^{(0)}+u^{\top}b^{(1)}}{2}.
\]
The assumed uniform convergence of the common parameter map \(\psi_n\) implies, at each \(\eta_k\),
\[
 b_{n,k}\longrightarrow b^{(k)}
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \Omega_{n,k}\longrightarrow\Omega,
 \qquad k\in\{0,1\}.
 \tag{2}
\]
In particular, positive definiteness of \(\Omega\) and (2) imply that there are constants \(c_{\Omega}>0\), \(C<\infty\), and \(n_0\) such that
\[
 c_{\Omega}\le
 \lambda_{\min}((\Omega_{n,k})_{bb})
 \le\lambda_{\max}((\Omega_{n,k})_{bb})\le C
 \qquad(k\in\{0,1\},\ n\ge n_0).
\tag{3}
\]
Moreover, since \(u^{\top}(b^{(1)}-b^{(0)})=d_b\), (2) gives, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 t-u^{\top}b_{n,0}\ge \frac{d_b}{4},
 \qquad
 u^{\top}b_{n,1}-t\ge \frac{d_b}{4}.
 \tag{4}
\]
Consider the test \(\varphi_n=\mathbf 1\{u^{\top}\widehat b_n>t\}\), which is measurable in the reduced observation defining \(\mathcal E_n^{\mathrm{mean}}\).  By (1)--(4) and Chebyshev's inequality,
\[
 \mathbb P_{n,\eta_0}(\varphi_n=1)
 \le \frac{16C}{n d_b^2}\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb P_{n,\eta_1}(\varphi_n=0)
 \le \frac{16C}{n d_b^2}\longrightarrow0.
 \tag{5}
\]
Let \(P^{\mathrm{mean}}_{n,k}\) be the law in the reduced experiment at \(\eta_k\).  With total variation defined as the supremum of probability differences over measurable events, (5) yields
\[
 \|P^{\mathrm{mean}}_{n,1}-P^{\mathrm{mean}}_{n,0}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \ge
 P^{\mathrm{mean}}_{n,1}(\varphi_n=1)
 -P^{\mathrm{mean}}_{n,0}(\varphi_n=1)
 \longrightarrow1.
 \tag{6}
\]
The reverse inequality is always at most one, so the limit in (6) equals one.

Now let \(G_k=N(m_k,\Omega)\) be the two laws in the frozen Gaussian experiment.  Set
\[
 a=\|\Omega^{-1/2}(m_1-m_0)\|_2.
\]
Because \(b^{(0)}\ne b^{(1)}\), the means differ, so \(a>0\); because both means are finite and \(\Omega\) is positive definite, \(a<\infty\).  To compute their total variation, whiten the observation and project it onto
\(\Omega^{-1/2}(m_1-m_0)/a\).  The log likelihood ratio is positive exactly when this scalar projection exceeds the midpoint of its two projected means.  Under the two laws, its centered distributions are standard normal and the projected means differ by \(a\).  Hence the likelihood-ratio half-space \(A^{\star}\) satisfies
\[
 G_1(A^{\star})-G_0(A^{\star})
 =\Phi(a/2)-\Phi(-a/2)
 =2\Phi(a/2)-1.
\]
The likelihood-ratio sign characterization also gives
\(\sup_A|G_1(A)-G_0(A)|=G_1(A^{\star})-G_0(A^{\star})\).  Therefore
\[
 \|G_1-G_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 =2\Phi(a/2)-1
 =v<1.
 \tag{7}
\]

Let \(K_n\) be any Markov kernel from the Gaussian observation space to the reduced-experiment observation space, and define
\[
 \varepsilon_n(K_n)
 =\sup_{\eta\in\mathcal K}
   \|K_nG_\eta-P^{\mathrm{mean}}_{n,\eta}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}.
\]
Total variation contracts under Markov kernels: indeed, for any output event \(B\), the map \(x\mapsto K_n(x,B)\) is measurable and lies in \([0,1]\), whence integration against \(G_1-G_0\) is bounded in absolute value by \(\|G_1-G_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\).  Thus the triangle inequality, contraction, and (7) imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \|P^{\mathrm{mean}}_{n,1}-P^{\mathrm{mean}}_{n,0}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 &\le
 \|P^{\mathrm{mean}}_{n,1}-K_nG_1\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 +\|K_nG_1-K_nG_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 +\|K_nG_0-P^{\mathrm{mean}}_{n,0}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\\
 &\le 2\varepsilon_n(K_n)+v.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{8}
\]
Combining (6) and (8) gives
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}\varepsilon_n(K_n)\ge\frac{1-v}{2}.
\]
Since (8) holds for every \(K_n\), it also holds after taking the infimum over kernels at each \(n\).  Therefore the deficiency from the frozen Gaussian experiment to \(\mathcal E_n^{\mathrm{mean}}\) obeys
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}
 \delta\!\left(\{G_\eta:\eta\in\mathcal K\},\mathcal E_n^{\mathrm{mean}}\right)
 \ge \frac{1-v}{2}>0.
\]
Asymptotic Le Cam equivalence would force both directional deficiencies to converge to zero, so it is impossible here.  The argument already assumes the requested convergence of \(\psi_n\) and uses neither a failure of QMD nor a failure of smoothing or tail control.  Equation (1) identifies the obstruction: the unscaled effect coordinates have variance of order \(n^{-1}\) and therefore reveal \(b\) asymptotically, whereas \(N((h,b),\Omega)\) retains nondegenerate effect-coordinate noise.  A compatible limit experiment must consequently observe \(b\) without noise while retaining Gaussian noise only in the root-\(n\)-scaled score coordinates, or else replace \(b\) by a genuinely local root-\(n\)-scaled effect parameter.
